about: Maps a component library to business types. For each business type it scores every section role 0-3; for each role it gives the page position, whether the role is a scroll section, and a best-first list of components. A generator can therefore choose, rank and order components without any heuristics of its own.
method: Roles derived from each component's MANIFEST type and display name. Need scored from sector homepage stacks, cross-checked against section frequency and mean page position across 144 DOM-coded homepages (100 Awwwards nominees, 44 ordinary business sites).

placementKinds.section: A band in the page scroll. Order by `position`.
placementKinds.chrome: Persistent UI (nav). Render once, outside the scroll.
placementKinds.entry: Renders before the page is revealed.
placementKinds.global: Triggered or layered, not placed in the stack.
placementKinds.internal: Tooling. Do not put on a customer-facing page.

typography.label: Kinetic type & text effects
typography.note: Usually a treatment inside the hero or a statement band.

gallery.label: Galleries, carousels, sliders
gallery.note: Work grid / lookbook. Moves up for visual products.

stats.label: Stats, counters & trust numbers
stats.note: Trust numbers. Earlier for lead-capture, later for portfolio.

form.label: Forms, search & booking
form.note: Contact / booking / newsletter. Near the end.

diagram.label: Diagrams, charts & dashboards
diagram.note: How-it-works. Moves up for abstract products.

overlay.label: Modals, toasts & tooltips
overlay.note: Modals, toasts, tooltips. Triggered, not placed.

loader.label: Loaders & preloaders
loader.note: Renders before the page; not part of the scroll.

utility.label: Calculators & tools
utility.note: Calculators sit with or just before pricing.

designsys.label: Design-system showcases
designsys.note: Design-system showcases. Not for customer pages.

local-service.label: Local service — trades, plumbing, HVAC, cleaning
local-service.goal: Get a call or a quote

why.stats: The trust strip (licensed, insured, years, rating) is a core section here, not decoration.
why.faq: FAQ runs 42% in lead-capture vs <23% in catalog — objection handling is the job.
why.map: Service-area coverage is a conversion blocker if missing.
why.background: Motion spend here reads as slow, not premium.

why.team: Named practitioners with credentials carry the trust load; a faceless clinic underperforms.
why.faq: Insurance and "what happens at the first visit" are top-3 visitor questions.
why.map: Locations, hours and parking are required.
why.background: Regulated sector — restraint reads as competence.

why.gallery: Visual proof is the product — the gallery sits high on the page.
why.pricing: Price transparency is expected; price lives in the service card title row.
why.feed: An Instagram feed is a genuine section here, not filler.
why.team: Clients book a person, not a premises.

why.map: Hours and address within one scroll is the #1 mobile intent.
why.product: The menu is the most-visited link — surface it, never bury it in nav.
why.gallery: Food and atmosphere carry the page; copy shrinks.
why.stats: Nobody books a table because you have 12 years of experience.

fitness.label: Fitness, gyms, studios, yoga
fitness.cta: Start free trial / Book a class

why.pricing: Membership tiers are expected on the homepage, unlike most local services.
why.stats: Member results are the proof; transformation numbers do the selling.
why.utility: BMI / calorie calculators are a real lead-capture device here.

why.process: "What happens after you contact us" outperforms feature talk — risk reduction is the whole job.
why.stats: Years, cases, awards, admissions. Outcomes beat adjectives.
why.gallery: There is nothing to photograph. Galleries are dead weight here.
why.background: Regulated claims need hedged copy and a sober page.

why.form: Search with location/type/price belongs in the hero.
why.map: Neighbourhood and location are the product.
why.stats: Sold, average days on market, volume — the agent's scoreboard.

why.faq: Counter-intuitive: FAQ is WEAK on storefronts (<23% of catalog-entry pages) and strong on service sites (42%). Objections get handled by the value-props strip, not an accordion.
why.cards: The value-props strip (shipping, returns, guarantee) is objection handling, not decoration.
why.overlay: Cart drawer, size guide, quick-view — overlays are functional here, not flourish.
why.feed: UGC / Instagram grid is standard merchandising.
why.product: Category tiles and best-seller rows are the page.

why.diagram: Abstract product — the how-it-works diagram moves up and copy grows.
why.features: Features run 72% of product-explainer pages, the highest of any section anywhere.
why.faq: 44% — objection handling before a pricing decision.
why.video: Product UI imagery is the hero asset; a stock photo signals immaturity.
why.designsys: You are selling software; a visible design system reads as craft.

why.typography: In award work the hero is a typographic statement — 17% typographic vs 5% split-hero.
why.background: WebGL/canvas is 14% of award heroes. Here the motion IS the portfolio.
why.loader: A preloader is a craft signal in this sector and nowhere else (14 of 100 award sites).
why.pricing: Naming a price is off-positioning for a studio.

why.gallery: The work grid or index-list IS the site. 70% of credibility-portfolio pages.
why.typography: Index-list layouts — text rows revealing images on hover — are the dominant era pattern.
why.faq: Almost never present. Fine artists drop CTAs nearly entirely.
why.nav: Minimal nav; often just a logo and a contact link.

why.form: The date-picker in the hero IS the section — everything else supports it.
why.gallery: Rooms, amenities, dining, the area. Visual product, copy shrinks.
why.map: "Getting here" is a real section for a destination property.
why.pricing: Book-direct incentive exists to fight OTAs and belongs above the fold.

why.stats: Outcome and placement numbers are the conversion lever.
why.pricing: Financing belongs beside pricing — cost is the top objection.
why.process: Format and "how it works" answer the commitment question.

why.gallery: Real-event galleries are the proof and the mood board at once.
why.pricing: Capacity, price band and dates are the three qualifying facts — hiding them creates junk leads.
why.typography: Single-purpose event pages are often a type-and-collage statement, not a stack.

why.stats: Impact numbers and financial transparency replace product proof.
why.testimonial: Stories from the field do what testimonials do elsewhere.
why.typography: High graphic personality; colour-block bands and slogan closers are common.
why.pricing: There is no price. Donation tiers live in the form.

why.feed: Latest grid, category rails, infinite scroll. Recency replaces merchandising.
why.section: Density is a feature — whitespace-heavy layouts mislead here.
why.hero: A lead-story block, not a marketing hero.
why.testimonial: Not a thing on a publisher homepage.

marketplace.label: Marketplace & two-sided platforms
marketplace.goal: Route each side to its funnel

why.process: How-it-works has to run once per side.
why.cards: Trust & safety is a required section, not optional.
why.loader: Skeletons matter — search results are the core interaction.
why.hero: The audience split must resolve above the fold or both sides bounce.

why.gallery: Device frames in a horizontal or pinned-scroll sequence carry the layout.
why.stats: Ratings and install counts are the proof.
why.video: Showing the app beats describing it.
